sheets.title:
Eschatology and Apocalypticism 

 Part 1 - Biblical Texts
Torah as a Source of Comfort
Isaiah 40- Haftarat Shabbat Nachamu (Pregaming fast days with "comfort Torah")
"Oft hope is born when all is forlorn": A Jewish Reading of Tolkien's Eucatastrophe
sheets.summary:
J.R.R. Tolkien coined the term “eucatastrophe” to refer to the sudden turn of events at the end of the story, which, at the very moment when all seems lost, offers joy, relief, and a happy ending. While he approached the term and its function from a Catholic perspective, this class will offer a glimpse into eucatastrophe in Jewish texts — as well as, of course, in your favorite works of Tolkien.

A source sheet for Shavuot Across Brooklyn.

description.en: Nature is discussed throughout Jewish literature in a variety of contexts. Many Jewish sources point to nature as a manifestation of godliness on earth, while others describe the importance of caring for our surroundings .
description.he: בספרות היהודית הטבע מופיע בהקשרים רבים. התבוננות בטבע מביאה להכרה בפלא בריאת העולם וביופי שבו. היהדות עוסקת בקשר של האדם והטבע, כאשר מצד אחד הוא כובש אותו ומצד שני שומר עליו. כמו כן, המקורות ספוגים בתיאורים ובדימויים רבים מעולם הטבע כמו: אפיקים בנגב ואייל עורג למים בספר תהילים, פריחת האביב בשיר השירים, משל האטד בספר שופטים ומשל הכרם של הנביא ישעיהו.

en.title: Renewal Through Trust

description.en: Hope is a defining theme of Jewish textual tradition. God’s [promises](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.15.5?ven=hebrew|Tanach_with_Ta%27amei_Hamikra&lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) to Abraham and Sarah, and to later patriarchs and matriarchs, inspired faith in a future that could not yet be seen, while the people of Israel's [redemption](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-exodus-from-egypt?tab=admin) from Egypt demonstrated that deep suffering can give way to freedom. During times of destruction and exile, prophets such as Jeremiah and Ezekiel sustained the people with visions of return, renewal, and restoration. This enduring hope continues to shape Jewish life today, finding expression in daily prayers for redemption and the declaration, often recited at the Passover seder, of “next year in Jerusalem.”

God is central in traditional Jewish texts. God [utters the world into existence](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.1.1?lang=bi&with=Translations&lang2=en) from the outset of Genesis, and Rambam, in the opening to his halakhic masterpiece, Mishnah Torah, explains that belief in God is the [foundation of all foundations](https://www.sefaria.org/Mishneh_Torah%2C_Foundations_of_the_Torah.1.1?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en). Countless Jewish sources discuss God's essence, the constraints of using human language to describe a transcendent Being, and how people are to develop relationships with God.

Isaiah, to whom the book of Isaiah is traditionally attributed, is one of the major biblical prophets. He is known for both prophesying the doom of Israel and its redemption — both politically and in a messianic age.
description.he: ישעיהו הוא אחד הנביאים החשובים במקרא, ומקובל לייחס לו את ספר ישעיהו. הוא נודע בזכות נבואות החורבן והגאולה שלו. נבואותיו משלבות מרכיבים פוליטיים ומשיחיים.

Rather it is a declaration of God's unity and other central doctrines of Judaism. It involves reciting three passages from the Torah, one of which is interrupted by another ancient phrase, the origins of which are outside the Bible.
description.he: קריאת שמע היא תפילה ידועה השגורה בפי עם ישראל והיא כוללת שלושה קטעים מפסוקי התורה ומשפט אחד שאינו מן התנ"ך. המילים של קריאת שמע הן הצהרה על ייחוד האל, אהבתו וקבלת עול מצוות. קריאת שמע היא מצווה מהתורה הנאמרת פעמיים ביום, בתפילת שחרית ובתפילת ערבית. רבים שמתו על קידוש השם קראו את קריאת שמע לפני מותם כהצהרה על אמונתם.

description.en: The opening two [chapters](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.1.1?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=he) of the Torah describe how God created the world in six days and rested on the seventh. These chapters are some of the most analyzed words in the Jewish textual tradition and serve as a basis for discussions of topics like [human dignity](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/human-dignity?tab=admin), God's role in the world, Shabbat, and humankind's responsibility for continuing the creation process and caring for the world.

en.title: The Unfathomable Wisdom of God
en.prompt: The Book of Isaiah, a cornerstone of prophetic literature, grapples with the themes of divine wisdom and the mystery of God's intentions.
en.ai_prompt: The prophets convey messages from God, yet even they cannot fully comprehend His divine plan. The Book of Isaiah, a cornerstone of prophetic literature, grapples with the themes of divine wisdom and the mystery of God's intentions.

description.en: Traditional Jewish sources [describe](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.14a.4?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en) how 48 prophets and seven prophetesses prophesied on behalf of the people of Israel. Many of their teachings are recorded in the Prophets section of the Bible, which consists of collections of prophetic speeches and narrative accounts of history attributed to prophets. These prophets covered the period from the people of Israel's entrance into the land of Israel through the beginning of the Second Temple. In the Torah, [Abraham](https://www.sefaria.org/Genesis.20.8?lang=bi&aliyot=0) and [Moses](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.34.10?lang=bi&aliyot=0) are also called prophets, and the Torah warns against listening to a [false prophet](https://www.sefaria.org/Deuteronomy.13.2?lang=bi&with=all&lang2=en).

Life is a fundamental value in Jewish texts. This value influences legal decisions, including end-of-life choices and when one is permitted to transgress other laws like Shabbat observance. The value placed on life raises questions about the meaning of life and how one should live one’s life, of which there are plentiful discussions in Jewish texts.

description.en: The prohibition against worshipping other gods is the second of the [Ten Commandments](https://www.sefaria.org/topics/the-ten-commandments?sort=Relevance&tab=sources), and one of the seven Noahide Laws, the laws the rabbis understood to be incumbent upon all non-Jews as well. That is, ideally, all the world recognizes God as the Creator and Master of the Universe. Nevertheless, worship of other gods is central to the dramatic relationship between God and Israel throughout the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible). Defining idolatry and ensuring that one does not inadvertently worship an idol or other god  is the core of the mishnaic and talmudic tractates of [Avodah Zarah](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah?tab=contents).

Vaetchanan (“I Pleaded”) opens as Moses describes his pleading with God to be allowed into the Land of Israel. Moses warns the Israelites not to pursue idolatry and recounts the giving of the Ten Commandments. The portion also contains the Shema, a declaration of faith and a central text in Jewish prayer.
description.he: בפרשת ואתחנן מתוארים תחנוני משה להיכנס לארץ. משה מזהיר את העם מפני עבודה זרה ומבדיל שלוש ערי מקלט בעבר הירדן המזרחי. הוא מזכיר גם את מעמד הר סיני, את עשרת הדברים ואת כתיבת לוחות הברית. בסוף הפרשה כתובה פרשת 'שמע ישראל', שהיא הצהרת אמונים מסורתית לאלוהי ישראל ושולבה לימים כחלק מרכזי בתפילה.

description.en: Tisha B’Av, the ninth day of the Hebrew month of Av, is a fast day and the saddest day on the Jewish calendar. Among other historical tragedies, it commemorates the destruction of the First and Second Temples in Jerusalem in 586 BCE and 70 CE, respectively. One fasting abstains from food and other physical pleasures, reads the biblical book of Lamentations, and observes mourning customs.
description.he: תשעה באב, החל בט' באב, הוא צום בן 25 שעות שיוצא בדרך כלל ביולי או אוגוסט. יום זה, המצוין על-ידי הימנעות מאכילה, שתייה, רחצה, יחסי מין ומלבושי עור, הוא יום של אבל על חורבן בית המקדש הראשון והשני בירושלים.

description.en: The High Holidays refer to the Jewish New Year (Rosh HaShanah) and the Day of Atonement (Yom Kippur) that follows 10 days later. These days are a time for repentance, introspection, prayer, and good deeds.
description.he: הימים הנוראים הם עשרת הימים שמראש השנה ועד יום כיפור. ימים אלו יכולים לשמש כזמן לתשובה, חשבון נפש, תפילה ומעשים טובים.

description.en: Lech Lecha (“Go Forth”) recounts Abraham’s (here known as Abram) first encounter with God, his journey to Canaan, the birth of his son Ishmael, the covenant between him, his descendants, and God, and God’s commandment to circumcise the males of his household.
description.he: בפרשת לך-לך מתוארת ההתגלות הראשונה של אלוהים לאברם. אברם יוצא עם אשתו שרי ובן אחיו לוט למסע במצוות אלוהים ומגיע לארץ כנען. שרי העקרה נותנת לאברם את שפחתה הגר. הגר יולדת את ישמעאל. אלוהים מצווה את אברם למול את עצמו ואת בני ביתו וכורת ברית עם אברם ועם זרעו. במסגרת הברית אלוהים משנה את שמו של אברם לאברהם ואת שמה של שרי לשרה.

en.title: Divine Comfort and Redemption
en.prompt: The divine assurance of comfort and the end of suffering for the people of Jerusalem serve as powerful messages of hope in Prophets, the second section of the Hebrew Bible. The book of Isaiah contains prophecies that shift from rebuke and warning to comfort and future redemption.
en.ai_prompt: The divine assurance of comfort and the end of suffering for the people of Jerusalem is a powerful message of hope and redemption. The book of Isaiah contains prophecies that shift from rebuke and warning to messages of comfort and future redemption.

description.en: Comfort appears in the Jewish tradition as an ease to be wished and prayed for, as a luxury to be wary of, and as an assistance to be offered to others. The act of comforting those in grief or distress in particular is a personal and communal obligation, and also a divine act. Halakhah (Jewish law) regulating mourning practices provides guidelines for mourners and their supporters receiving and giving comfort after the death of a close family member. In the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible), prophets such as Isaiah and Jeremiah preach prophecies of comfort in response to national catastrophes (as well as prophecies of rebuke and warning in advance of them). Certain such prophecies of consolation from the book of Isaiah are traditionally read publicly in the seven weeks following the communal mourning day of Tisha B’Av.

The act of comforting those in grief or distress in particular is a personal and communal obligation, and also a divine act. Halakhah (Jewish law) regulating mourning practices provides guidelines for mourners and their supporters receiving and giving comfort after the death of a close family member. In the Tanakh (Hebrew Bible), prophets such as Isaiah and Jeremiah preach prophecies of comfort in response to national catastrophes (as well as prophecies of rebuke and warning in advance of them). Certain such prophecies of consolation from the book of Isaiah are traditionally read publicly in the seven weeks following the communal mourning day of Tisha B’Av.

Vaetchanan (“I Pleaded”) opens as Moses describes his pleading with God to be allowed into the Land of Israel. Moses warns the Israelites not to pursue idolatry and recounts the giving of the Ten Commandments. The portion also contains the Shema, a declaration of faith and a central text in Jewish prayer.

description.he: ד"ר מרטין לותר קינג הבן היה כומר אמריקאי ומנהיג התנועה האפרו־אמריקאית לזכויות האזרח בשנות השישים של המאה העשרים. קינג תמך במדינת ישראל ולחם לצידו של הרב אברהם יהושע השל נגד האנטישמיות בתקופת פעילותה של התנועה לזכויות האזרח.
description.en: Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. was an American reverend and leader of the American Civil Rights Movement in the 1960s. King advocated for Israel’s security and fought against antisemitism during the Civil Rights Movement alongside Rabbi Abraham Joshua Heschel.
